def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S₀ S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S₀ Fm] [Entailment S Fm]
    (𝓑 : S₀) (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓑] [Entailment.Cl 𝓢] (K F : Fm → Fm),
    Def1 𝓑 𝓢 K → Def2 𝓢 K → Def4 𝓢 K →
    𝓑 ⊢ F (∼F ⊥) 🡒 F ⊥ →
    (∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K (K φ 🡒 F φ)) →
    𝓢 ⊢ K (∼K (∼F ⊥))

translation: Target is the following proposition. For every choice of types Fm, S₀ and S, of logical connectives and truth and falsehood constants on Fm, and of provability relations for S₀ and S on Fm, take any 𝓑 : S₀ and 𝓢 : S. Assume that each system proves all classical propositional tautologies and is closed under modus ponens. Then for every pair of functions K, F : Fm → Fm, the following successive hypotheses imply the conclusion: (1) for every sentence φ, if 𝓑 proves φ, then 𝓢 proves K(φ); (2) for every sentence φ and every sentence ψ, 𝓢 proves the sentence K(φ 🡒 ψ) 🡒 (K(φ) 🡒 K(ψ)); (3) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves the sentence K(K(φ) 🡒 φ); (4) 𝓑 proves the sentence F(∼(F(⊥))) 🡒 F(⊥); and (5) for every sentence φ, 𝓢 proves the sentence K(K(φ) 🡒 F(φ)). The conclusion is that 𝓢 proves the sentence K(∼(K(∼(F(⊥))))). In (3) and (5) the outer K applies to the whole implication; the implications without that outer K are not required as hypotheses. There is no hypothesis of consistency, no general rule assumed from 𝓢 proving φ to 𝓢 proving K(φ), and no requirement of a sentence ψ for which 𝓑 proves ψ 🡘 ∼(F(ψ)).

divergences.description: The source assumes that S includes EA. The target does not require that every theorem of 𝓑 is a theorem of 𝓢. Def1 gives 𝓢 ⊢ K φ from 𝓑 ⊢ φ, not 𝓢 ⊢ φ; Def4 gives known factivity, not a rule for removing that K.

The target adds the premise 𝓑 ⊢ F(∼F ⊥) 🡒 F ⊥. The printed theorem imposes the pointwise capture condition on F but does not require EA to prove this further implication. Even if intended as a repair, the premise materially restricts the result.

The declared abstraction replaces EA and its syntax with an arbitrary classical base and sentence type. In particular, F is any sentence function, not necessarily application of a single one-free-variable arithmetic formula to sentence numerals. The target does not express arithmetic definability, Gödel coding, or the distinction between Σ⁰₁ and more complex formulas.
The target fixes Con(F) to mean ∼F ⊥, whereas the passage uses Con(F) without specifying its expansion there.

Def1, Def2, and Def4 make knowledge of the base, closure of knowledge under modus ponens, and known factivity explicit hypotheses on the abstract K. The quoted theorem does not list these as separate hypotheses.

judgement.summary: The pointwise capture hypothesis and the nesting of K and negation in the conclusion match the passage under the stated reading of Con(F). The target nevertheless omits theory inclusion and assumes an additional base-provable implication about F, so it is not the theorem as printed.
